articles.headline: Ministry of Education Launches New Curriculum Framework for Primary Schools
articles.preview: The Malawi Ministry of Education has unveiled a new curriculum framework aimed at improving literacy and numeracy outcomes across primary schools nationwide.
articles.content:
The Malawi Ministry of Education has unveiled a new curriculum framework aimed at improving literacy and numeracy outcomes across primary schools nationwide.

The framework, developed in consultation with teachers' unions and education researchers, places a stronger emphasis on foundational reading and mathematics skills in the early grades, with revised teaching guides expected to reach schools ahead of the next academic year.

Officials say the changes respond directly to national assessment data showing gaps in early-grade literacy, and that additional teacher training will accompany the rollout.

articles.headline: Government Announces Increased Bursary Support for Rural Teachers
articles.preview: New funding will help cover accommodation and transport costs for teachers posted to hard-to-reach rural schools starting next term.
articles.content:
New funding will help cover accommodation and transport costs for teachers posted to hard-to-reach rural schools starting next term.

The support package is intended to ease the burden on teachers serving in remote areas, where housing and transport have long been cited as major barriers to staff retention.

Education officials say the initiative is part of a broader effort to reduce teacher turnover in rural districts.

articles.headline: PSLCE Marking Guidelines Updated for 2025
articles.preview: MANEB has released updated marking guidelines for the Primary School Leaving Certificate Examination, with revised rubrics for continuous assessment.
articles.content:
MANEB has released updated marking guidelines for the Primary School Leaving Certificate Examination, with revised rubrics for continuous assessment.

The changes are designed to bring greater consistency to how continuous assessment marks are combined with final examination scores.

Schools have been asked to review the new guidelines ahead of the next marking cycle.
